description: Your Juris-M library contains 12 court cases from three jurisdictions (United States, United Kingdom, and Canada) that need to be organized for a comparative constitutional law course. The cases are in a flat, unorganized list with several errors. You must: (1) Create a parent collection named 'Comparative Constitutional Law' containing three subcollections named exactly 'US Cases', 'UK Cases', and 'Canada Cases'. (2) Assign each of the 12 cases to its correct subcollection based on its jurisdiction — check the reporter and court fields to determine jurisdiction. (3) Three US cases are missing their court field — identify these cases (they are well-known SCOTUS cases) and set the court to 'United States Supreme Court'. Two cases (one US, one UK) have the court set to 'Unknown Court' — correct these to the proper court name ('United States Supreme Court' for the US case, 'House of Lords' for the UK case). (4) Tag all US cases with 'United States', all UK cases with 'United Kingdom', and all Canadian cases with 'Canada'. Login: username 'ga', password 'password123'.
